title: Invoice currency casing

change.goal: Show uppercase currency codes in invoice lists, pages, and CSV exports.
change.why: Some older invoices display lower-case currency codes.
parts: Add currency normalization with a three-code allowlist and fallback
Format list and page prices independently

verdict:
The change does not satisfy the task.
- Archived currencies remain lower-case in CSV.
- Invoice pages relabel valid currencies outside USD, EUR and GBP as USD.
now: The list uppercases its own price, the page applies an allowlist and fallback, and CSV exports the original currency. Both screens duplicate amount formatting.
target: Uppercase the archive currency when readArchive adapts archived rows; the installed service client already guarantees uppercase. Restore the shared formatPrice for both screens and leave CSV consuming the normalized invoices. Preserve the original currency and amount without inventing defaults.
recommendation: Reshape toward normalization at the archive boundary and restore shared price formatting.

steps.text: Normalize archived currency on ingestion, and remove the allowlist and invented fallback while restoring shared screen formatting.
Test both invoice sources across the list, page, and CSV, including an accepted currency outside the allowlist.

requirements.text: Show the currency code in uppercase in the invoice list.
requirements.not_checked: Visual rendering in the desktop application; output strings were exercised directly.

requirements.text: Show the invoice's currency code in uppercase on the invoice page.
requirements.not_checked: Visual rendering in the desktop application.

requirements.text: Show the invoice's currency code in uppercase in CSV export.
Handle invoices from the billing service and the local archive.

findings.title: The page silently changes valid currencies to USD
findings.what: The allowlist substitutes USD for valid three-letter codes outside USD, EUR and GBP, changing the represented currency rather than just its case. The page applies this to both service and archive invoices.
findings.shown_by: A direct run through loadInvoices and renderPage produced USD 10.00 for both a service invoice with CAD and an archive row with cad; list output was CAD 10.00. The service's installed validator accepts CAD (node_modules/@acme/billing-client/index.js:3-14), and data/archive.schema.json:9 accepts cad.
findings.fix: Preserve the code and uppercase the archived value at its adapter; remove the allowlist and USD fallback, and use the shared formatter on the page.

findings.title: CSV still exports archived currency in lower case
findings.what: Uppercasing only in screen paths leaves the CSV consumer with the unmodified archive currency, so the required export remains incorrect.
findings.shown_by: A direct run through loadInvoices and toCsv exported A,cad,10.00 for an archive row with cur cad; src/export/csv.js:2 reads invoice.currency directly.
findings.fix: Uppercase row.cur in readArchive so CSV and both screens consume the same normalized invoice; the service client already guarantees uppercase.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the page or CSV paths
findings.what: The added tests cover the helper and list only, and explicitly expect an unsupported fallback. They do not exercise either source through all three outputs or check preservation of a code outside the allowlist.
findings.shown_by: npm test passes all four tests while the direct CAD/cad reproduction demonstrates both the incorrect page and lower-case CSV.
findings.fix: Add tests using an accepted service code and a lowercase archive code, asserting that list, page and CSV preserve the code in uppercase; replace tests that require fabricated USD fallback.

units.name: normalizeCurrency
jobs: For non-string or blank input returns the fallback; otherwise trims and uppercases, then returns the result only for USD/EUR/GBP, else fallback
units.reason: The input contracts already guarantee strings and the allowlist changes valid currencies; archive adaptation supplies needed case conversion.

units.name: renderList
jobs: Maps invoices to number and amount formatted in major units; substitutes USD for nullish currency then uppercases it
units.reason: Restore its shared formatter after normalization at the input boundary.

units.name: renderPage
jobs: Normalizes the code and formats the amount; on any exception returns a fabricated USD zero price; returns the invoice title and price
units.reason: Restore shared formatting and avoid unsupported substitutions and exception masking.

units.name: formatPrice
jobs: Formats currency and amount in major units

units.name: loadInvoices
jobs: Combines validated service invoices with adapted archive rows

units.name: readArchive
jobs: Maps stored archive row fields into invoice fields without changing currency

units.name: toCsv
jobs: Serializes the invoice currency and amount directly

mechanisms.name: Screen-level currency normalization and fallback
mechanisms.purpose: Uppercase currencies for screen prices and fall back to USD for selected unexpected inputs.
mechanisms.basis: Task requires uppercase at all three outputs (../brief.md:3); archive strings are required lowercase in data/archive.schema.json:5-10 and service strings are validated uppercase in node_modules/@acme/billing-client/index.js:3-14. Weight is unassessed because blocks also contain shared price-formatting work.
mechanisms.instead: src/invoices/archive.js:2-3 is the adapter through which archive currency enters all outputs; src/invoices/load.js:5-6 combines it with service results, whose uppercase contract is validated at node_modules/@acme/billing-client/index.js:11-14.
mechanisms.benefit: Screen uppercase for archive inputs; fallback would display a price for invalid or absent currency, whose occurrence is unknown and excluded by the documented source contracts.
mechanisms.cost: Different screen rules and duplicated amount formatting leave CSV unnormalized, relabel accepted currencies, and hide page errors with a fabricated price.
mechanisms.decision: Replace screen-level conversions and fallbacks with uppercase conversion at the archive adapter; reuse the existing shared price formatter. This preserves valid source codes across all outputs without claiming support for invalid inputs.

blocks.does: Defines the allowed currency list and fallback-based normalizer.
